designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Reads instantly as a stamp from 3 m: clean perforated edge, double rule frame, a well-proportioned header band with widely tracked serif caps 'PISA' balanced by '3.97°' as the denomination. Using the lean angle as the face value is a smart joke that rewards a second look. The leaning tower against the strict vertical frame gives the composition its tension, and the paving band anchors the bottom. It holds up as one ink on both white and black. Weaknesses: stroke weight is uneven, with the upper storeys and belfry dense and heavy while the base storey is drawn in thin hairlines, so the tower looks top-heavy and the top may fill in on black. The tower's base line is tilted, so the left foot floats above the ground band instead of sitting on it. '3.97°' is set tighter than the airy 'PISA', and the period crowds the 3.
designs.fix: Even out the tower's line weight (lighten the lattice on the belfry and upper storeys, or bring the base storey up to the same weight) and sit the base flush on the paving line, so the tower reads as a single drawing planted on the ground. Also open up the tracking on '3.97°' a little to match 'PISA'.
